speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of the swelling in your right knee, and has it been accompanied by pain or difficulty moving the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multicentric Retinohistiocytosis (MCRH) - Wait, that doesn't fit the knee symptoms. Based on the age, spontaneous right knee swelling without trauma, and strong family history of similar joint issues, this is highly suggestive of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA), specifically the oligoarticular type. However, given the specific family history pattern, could this be a hereditary bone or cartilage disorder like Ollier disease or Maffucci syndrome? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right_Knee. REQUEST IMAGES
